definition: MLX is an open-source machine learning framework developed by Apple and designed primarily for Apple silicon.
details: It is used for training and running machine learning models and is optimized for Apple silicon's unified memory architecture, allowing the CPU and GPU to work with the same data without copying it between separate memory pools. MLX can be used for applications including large language model training and inference, image generation, and speech recognition.

explainer.lead: MLX is Apple's open-source machine learning framework designed primarily for Apple silicon. It matters because it exploits unified memory so CPU and GPU share data without copying.

tiers.eli5: It's a tool built for a particular kind of Apple chip so the processor and graphics unit can work on the same material without making copies.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for training and running models, including large language model training and inference, image generation and speech recognition. A pitfall is hardware scope: it is designed primarily for Apple silicon rather than general hardware.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-source machine learning framework from Apple, designed primarily for Apple silicon and optimized for its unified memory architecture, where CPU and GPU work on the same data without copying between separate memory pools.

explainer.example: A developer runs speech recognition on an Apple silicon device, with the framework keeping data in shared unified memory.
